drafted_from: tools/pin-files-by-content/tool-rows.json (tool:pin-files-by-content), do-work/pin-files.mjs, read-data/pins.mjs and pin-shape.json, test/pin-files-by-content.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check whether the pins in pins.json still match the files in my settings folder, and tell me which are stale." It runs pin-files.mjs check on your computer and names every file whose pin is added, changed or gone.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads a folder of files and one pin file on your computer and answers which pins differ.
instructions: 1. Clone the Workshop repository and run npm install in it (the tool needs @noble/hashes), then work from its root.
2. Say which folder holds the files to pin and which pin file records them; the AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:pin-files-by-content"}.

3. It runs "node tools/pin-files-by-content/do-work/pin-files.mjs check --root <root> --pin-file <pin file> --folder <folder>", adding --unpinned-ok <file> once for each file that is never pinned (for example package.json).

4. Read the one JSON line it prints: ok, pinned, added, changed, gone, unchanged, written. Exit 1 means a difference; exit 2 means a path or the pin file could not be read, with the reason on standard error.
5. When you mean the files to be the new truth, run the same command with write in place of check, then commit the pin file in the same change as the files.

worked_examples.title: Check a settings folder against an empty pin file
worked_examples.ask: Check whether pins.json matches my settings folder.
worked_examples.given: From tools/pin-files-by-content/test/pin-files-by-content.test.mjs (the first test): a folder settings holding colors.json ({"sky":"blue"}), themes/night.json and package.json, and a pins.json with an empty "files" object. The AI runs: node tools/pin-files-by-content/do-work/pin-files.mjs check --root /work/app --pin-file pins.json --folder settings --unpinned-ok package.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"ok":false,"pinned":2,"added":["colors","themes/night"],"changed":[],"gone":[],"unchanged":0,"written":false} with exit 1, and nothing written. Running the same line with write answers written true and exit 0; a check after that answers ok true, and pins.json then holds, for colors, {"path":"colors.json","pin":{"bytes":15,"blake3":"<64 hex digits>"}}.
